bounded_search_quality_check.method: four representative scientific phrases sent through the Phase 1 source-native adapters; at most five normalized results inspected per source and query; no tuning performed

NSF.observation: all inspected awards were directly relevant

NIH.observation: all inspected projects were strongly relevant

NSF.observation: all inspected awards were strongly relevant

NIH.observation: top projects were glioblastoma-relevant, but their displayed title/abstract snippets did not consistently evidence every query concept

bounded_search_quality_check.conclusion: Source-native search is adequate for a Phase 2 standalone product when users choose source-appropriate, reasonably precise scientific phrases.
material_weaknesses: NIH native ordering can broaden multi-concept searches toward the disease area without making every query-concept match visible in the first displayed records.
NSF and NIH relevance scores are not exposed or comparable, so the product keeps source sections and does not imply a global cross-source rank.
Zero results from the other agency can reflect legitimate source-domain specificity rather than a retrieval failure.

known_limitations: Eligibility is intentionally conservative: an NSF solicitation without an exact or reviewed program-element mapping does not receive a funded-awards link.

The reviewed CPS and translational-program groups include explicit historical parent/predecessor program elements because newly assigned 2026 program elements do not yet provide meaningful award history.

Each source returns at most 25 normalized records per page; NIH broad searches scan at most 12 RePORTER pages to establish the requested normalized-project page and do not speculate that a further page exists when that bounded scan cannot establish a lookahead.
The standalone product reports source-native order and does not claim comparable relevance between NSF and NIH.
The public Award API deployment is intentionally deferred to the protected post-merge workflow; the pull request must stop before merge for review.

rollback.product: Revert funded_awards.html and its dedicated assets; the existing Funding Finder and Team Match pages remain independent.
rollback.integration: Revert assets/award-links.js and the small assets/app.js link renderer addition; current opportunity ranking and rendering remain otherwise unchanged.
rollback.worker: Set AWARD_API_ENABLED=false or roll back the Worker version captured by the protected deployment workflow.
